newsitem.title: USA: CSCE October sugar soars on fund buying - trade.
newsitem.headline: CSCE October sugar soars on fund buying - trade.

text.p: CSCE October sugar contract soared to its highest level since late January 1995 due to waves of fund buying, though the gains met with some selling on the highs, traders said.
"It's been all fund buying between October and March. Some 5,000 lots of fund buy stops were touched off," a floor source said. "I have heard of no physical news, this is all purely technical."
October sugar rose to a high of 12.15 cents per pound, just short of 12.20 cents per pound close on January 26, 1995.
March, May and July 1997 contracts also reached new highs.
At 1307 October sugar was up 0.34 cent at 12.12 cents, traded 12.16 to 11.75 cents.
March was up 0.23 cent at 11.66 cents, off the high of 11.67 cents. May was up 0.16 cent at 11.39 cents, with July up 0.15 cent at 11.05 cents.
Traders said light buy stops were triggered at 12.08 basis October and 11.63 basis March.
"There is plenty of producer and trade selling around the highs, but more fund buying is coming in," a trader said.
